selectionRule: Admitting an evaluated design to the archive does not mean it is the best design. Read the design account, inspect its resources, and compare the final archived selection.

archive.account: The harness this run started from

This agent keeps the minimal shell tool and adds a final-answer verifier middleware plus context-QA prompting. The system prompt and skill now instruct the model to read the entire supplied context, bridge facts across paragraphs, copy exact names/numbers/dates, and obey "return only the short answer" formatting. The new verifier runs before every final answer: a side LLM compares the candidate answer against the question and supplied context, accepts it if it is exact and supported, replaces it with the corrected context wording when it is abbreviated/paraphrased/over-explained, or sends the main agent back with targeted feedback. This should raise held-out exact-match accuracy by fixing near-miss answers (missing middle names, added units, explanatory prefixes) and catching unsupported short answers, without adding web tools that are unnecessary for supplied-context tasks and could distract the agent or fail startup validation.

archive.account: This agent keeps the shell tool and the final-answer gate, but replaces the single-shot verifier with a message-aware extract-then-verify ensemble. A before_llm hook snapshots the exact user/tool messages the main model saw, so the gate reads the real supplied context and shell output instead of relying only on ctx.question. At final-answer time it runs three independent side-LLM extractors over that context, using varied answer-type and multi-hop prompts to return exact answer substrings plus supporting quotes; it forms a reference answer by agreement voting (exact first, then normalized). If the main candidate matches the reference after normalization, the gate adopts the exact-context wording; if the candidate conflicts, a judge side LLM picks between the candidate and the extracted alternatives, with the reference's agreement strength stated so weak single-extractor hints are not over-trusted. Forced answers go through the same gate. The system prompt and skill are tightened around verbatim-span copying for numbers, dates, names, and units, and around using shell only when the supplied context lacks the answer. I expect higher exact-match accuracy because the gate gets a grounded, consensus-extracted reference rather than one judge that may be anchored by a near-miss candidate, and because it can see the actual task context and tool output.

archive.account: This agent keeps the shell tool but replaces the final-answer gate with a span-lock verifier. A before_llm hook snapshots the exact user/tool messages the main model saw, so the gate judges the real supplied context rather than only ctx.question. Before accepting any final answer it runs one side-LLM semantic verdict, then programmatically checks that the accepted or corrected wording exists as a literal span of that evidence. The span matcher is case/punctuation/accent-insensitive, enforces token boundaries, returns the verbatim context substring, and when several occurrences share the same normalized characters it prefers the one closest to the candidate's original spelling/punctuation. If a verdict correction is paraphrased or not literal, a single exact-span extractor re-reads the context once as a fallback, and a conservative relatedness heuristic (same tokens reordered, missing middle initials, small fuller/shorter forms) repairs wording without the multi-extractor voting/judge machinery that previously over-corrected. Accepted-but-not-literal candidates are either locked to a related literal span or kept on semantic acceptance, so yes/no and other non-span answers are not forced into fake spans. The system prompt and skill instruct the model to treat the context as the source of one contiguous answer span and to copy revisions verbatim. I expect this to score higher because final answers are programmatically locked to supplied-context wording, reducing omitted middle names, paraphrases, and formatting drift, while using fewer side-LLM calls and fewer unjustified rewrites than the prior ensemble gate.

archive.account: This agent keeps a span-lock final-answer gate, but the verifier now separates the actual question from the supplied context, localizes evidence against that question, and gives the side LLM the question explicitly. Before the semantic verdict, it splits the exact user/tool evidence into passages, scores them by lexical overlap with the question and the current candidate, and passes an order-preserving focused subset around the likely answer to both the verifier and the exact-span extractor. The extractor reads those localized passages but anchors its output against the full evidence, so it can only return a verbatim context span. When the main agent is sent back, the revision feedback contains the retrieved exact context passages rather than a generic instruction. The gate also strips answer-prefix labels and list/markdown formatting from the candidate, normalizes yes/no to lowercase before span-locking (so an uppercase "Yes" in the evidence cannot override the requested lowercase format), and accepts a shorter/fuller correction only when the side LLM has already rejected the candidate. I expect higher exact-match accuracy because the verifier and extractor actually see the supporting region and the real question rather than truncated context or a question-less clip, so corrections are better grounded and more often literal spans, while revision feedback gives the main model the exact wording to copy.

archive.account: This agent keeps the span-lock final gate but adds a deterministic `span_lookup` tool the main model calls before finalizing, so it copies verbatim context spans instead of relying only on post-hoc repair. The gate now also performs soft span-locking: near-miss phrases like "John Kennedy" or "J. F. Kennedy" are expanded to the shortest context span containing their tokens in order ("John Fitzgerald Kennedy"), using initial-aware token matching with a small gap budget. It robustly strips answer-prefix/list formatting, including bold `ANSWER:` labels and echoed `[span_lookup] EXACT SPAN:`/`NEAR SPAN:` output (both multi-line and compact same-line echoes), keeps yes/no lowercase, treats explicit BAD/WRONG/INCORRECT verdicts as revision requests even when bold/underscore-wrapped, lets the LLM extractor fall back to soft spans, filters span-lookup echoes from the evidence pool, and gates the forced-answer path using a refreshed message snapshot. I expect higher exact-match because more answers are corrected to exact context wording both before the main model finalizes and again by the final gate, including edge cases where the model echoes the lookup tool or emits formatting around the answer.

archive.account: This agent makes the main model finish with a self-cited EVIDENCE/ANSWER block, then gates that citation. The final gate parses the model's own supporting sentence(s), programmatically verifies they are verbatim spans of the supplied context, and runs the side-LLM verifier against that focused cited evidence (with only the actual question text, not the full distractor context) rather than the whole paragraph set. If the candidate is not literally present in the cited evidence (or no valid citation is given), it falls back to the original full-context span-lock verifier. It lowercases yes/no before span-locking and, for accepted answers, returns a replace action so the final output is only the cleaned short answer, never the raw EVIDENCE/ANSWER block or an answer-prefix label. This should score higher because the model localizes supporting evidence for multi-hop questions, the verifier is less distracted by irrelevant paragraphs, and the final answer is still locked to exact context wording.

archive.account: This agent keeps the shell tool and a span-lock final gate, but adds reference-first boundary calibration. Before judging, it runs an independent exact-span extractor over the real evidence the main model saw. If the main candidate is already a literal context span but is a too-short title prefix (e.g. "Air Italy" vs "Air Italy S.p.A.", "Christian Clemenson" vs "Christian Dayton Clemenson") or carries extra leading/trailing words (e.g. "the Dallas Cowboys...", "Big 12 Conference", "140 acre"), the gate deterministically replaces it with the independently extracted span when the two are small fuller/shorter forms of each other. Calibration is restricted to boundary changes: for two literal spans it never reorders accepted wording. A second boundary-focused extractor is used only when the candidate is a title prefix (including markdown list-item labels), so ordinary correct spans are not challenged. Yes/no is normalized to lowercase before span-locking, and the system prompt/skill instruct the model to choose full names over title prefixes and to avoid extra articles, units, and suffixes. I expect higher exact-match accuracy because this directly fixes the most common span-lock failure—literal but wrong-boundary answers—without the over-correction of full ensemble judges.

archive.account: This agent keeps the reference-first span-lock gate, but adds deterministic answer-shape contracts before the side-LLM verdict: "How many X?" answers reduce to the numeral, "When/What year" answers strip leading prepositions and stacked prefixes plus trailing sentence punctuation, and cleaned candidates are emitted via replace so labels/whitespace never survive an accept. The same contracts are applied to the independently extracted reference span, and boundary calibration is shape-aware so a contracted count/date answer cannot be re-expanded to a qualified phrase. It also adds a composite multi-span locker: when the whole candidate is not a literal span but contains a conjunction/list separator, it locks each constituent to a verbatim context span and reassembles them with the candidate's own separators, including punctuation attached to pieces. The boundary-calibration guard is tightened so multi-part answers cannot be over-trimmed to a single-token reference. I expect a higher exact-match score because this fixes failure classes the prior single-span gate left open—multi-item answers assembled from non-adjacent evidence and count/date formatting drift—without adding broad multi-extractor over-correction.

It also adds a composite multi-span locker: when the whole candidate is not a literal span but contains a conjunction/list separator, it greedily locks each constituent to a verbatim context span and reassembles them with the candidate's separators. archive.account: This agent adds abductive proof-obligation verification on top of evidence-table extraction. It parses each question into a query frame (target type, requested relation, constraints, output form), builds a scoped fact table from every snippet, and restricts candidates to the type the question actually asks for (with explicit yes/no candidates and derived numeric candidates when needed). For each candidate it then derives the proof obligations that must hold if that candidate were the answer and scores them with explicit positive support, contradiction, assumption, and constraint-violation penalties, followed by a reverse-question confirmation and a strict bare-answer output contract. I expect it to score higher because type-restricted candidates and backward-chaining proof obligations suppress wrong-type and unsupported-but-plausible answers more reliably than forward candidate search alone, while the reverse confirmation and output sanitizer reduce format and type errors.

archive.account: This agent now pairs a deterministic UserPromptSubmit pre-rank hook with a span-locked multi-reasoner adjudication skill. The hook parses the standard Context/Question wrapper, scores every evidence line by question-token overlap with a rare-word bonus, and injects a deduplicated top-ranked evidence view before the model reads the full context; any parse failure no-ops. The skill then builds a word-for-word evidence ledger separating exact rows from distractors, runs three independent readers (forward retrieval, backward chaining, adversarial falsification), and adjudicates by consensus. The final answer must be a verbatim contiguous span copied byte-for-byte from the strongest evidence, exactly yes/no or choice text, or—only for arithmetic questions with no verbatim span—a number computed from exact ledger values. I expect higher scores because the hook weakens first-snippet ordering bias before reasoning starts, the independent-perspective vote cancels single-pass errors, and exact-span copying (with a traceable arithmetic escape hatch) preserves exact-match points without forcing spans on derived numbers.

archive.account: This agent upgrades the previous pre-rank hook into a deterministic evidence-map hook that works at sentence level even for HotpotQA-style "Title: paragraph" lines. It parses the supplied Context/Question wrapper, extracts copyable candidate spans (dates, numbers, quoted strings, choice letters, multiword names, and title-case phrases such as "Night of the Black Snow"), builds a query-focused entity graph that propagates relevance up to two hops, and injects a QUERY FRAME + CANDIDATE BOARD + EXPANDED EVIDENCE ahead of the full context. Question-mentioned spans are aggressively demoted so the board shortlists answer-shaped spans rather than constraints, and the expanded evidence preserves the exact answer-bearing sentence instead of truncating it away. The skill treats that map as a shortlist, builds a coreference-resolved evidence ledger from the complete context, verifies each candidate with forward retrieval, backward chaining, explicit graph chaining for bridge questions, and proof-obligation/falsification scoring, then copies the winning span byte-for-byte. I expect it to score higher because the sentence-level graph and title-case extraction directly target missed second-hop evidence and non-verbatim spans, while the full-context verification step prevents the injected shortlist from becoming a new bias.

This agent adds a deterministic evidence-map preprocessor as a UserPromptSubmit hook, then makes the skill verify every injected span instead of trusting it. The hook parses the Context/Question wrapper, splits evidence into sentence units with abbreviation-safe boundaries (St., U.S., Dec., etc.), strips list markers so they never become fake sentences, and extracts copyable candidates (names, compound places, dates, digit/word numbers, quotes, choice letters, title-case phrases). It injects a query frame, a candidate board with supporting lines, and expanded evidence.

Two deterministic readers sit on top. A slot-fill resolver aligns the question's content words to an evidence sentence and cuts the exact answer surface by question shape: subject or passive by-agent for WHO, date for WHEN, the object after the relation for WHERE/WHAT, and the numeric core for HOW MANY (returning "5" rather than "5 albums", and "5 million" rather than "5 million people"). It trims trailing date adjuncts, rejects pronoun-only guesses, and resolves WHERE back-references such as "born there" to the preceding location sentence. A comparison resolver extracts the compared entities and their values, but now prefers the attribute named in the question (e.g. "points" in "more points") over unrelated birth dates, and marks a provisional winner only after re-deriving direction.

The skill treats all injected spans as hypotheses that must pass a slot-fill test against the full context ledger and be copied byte-for-byte only after verification. I expect a higher score because the deterministic readers directly target the exact-boundary, HOW-MANY over-copy, comparison-attribute, date-abbreviation, list-marker, and coreference errors that remain near the leader's level, while full-context verification prevents the injected shortlist from becoming a new source of bias.

archive.account: This agent keeps full-context evidence verification but changes both the preprocessor and the final surface-selection rules. The UserPromptSubmit hook now injects explicit two-sentence BRIDGE PATH WITNESSES and builds the evidence graph with morphological/country aliases (demonym/place and singular/plural variants), so second-hop lines that share no exact question word are surfaced before reasoning. It also extracts digit-containing proper names and category phrases, and tags each board candidate with a TITLE/FIRST/OBJECT surface-role hint. The skill then separates entity selection from surface selection: after verifying the winning entity, it copies the answer surface from the sentence that actually fills the question's slot. Type-specific rules keep full person names, keep official organization/conference names including legal suffixes (dropping a final category word only when the question already qualifies that category, such as "which Division II conference" → "Northeast-10" rather than "Northeast-10 Conference"), trim nested place phrases to the requested granularity, and copy bare category/date/quantity forms. I expect it to score higher because the prior leader's residual errors are concentrated in missed alias-only bridge hops and exact-span boundary mistakes, and this design targets both without the rigid deterministic slot-fill readers that regressed the last attempt.
